Malzahar.escape: Malzahar has no mobility, so the moment after you break P Void Shift and the silence from Q Call of the Void ends is your chance to engage. When R Nether Grasp has already been used or an ally can interrupt its cast, close the gap with Yone E Soul Unbound and tornado Q Mortal Steel.
Malzahar.build: Prioritize magic resistance against Malzahar Q Call of the Void, W Void Swarm, and E Malefic Visions. Consider Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar to counter Malzahar R Nether Grasp.
Malzahar.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, then break Malzahar P Void Shift first with a regular Q. If you can all-in safely, deal damage with Yone E Soul Unbound → tornado Q Mortal Steel → basic attack → W Spirit Cleave → R Fate Sealed → basic attack, then return with E Soul Unbound. If Malzahar can use R Nether Grasp, suppression may prevent your return, so don’t go deep with this combo alone.
Malzahar.fight: If Malzahar P Void Shift is active, break it first with Yone Q Mortal Steel, then engage. Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, and go in when you can avoid the silence from Malzahar Q Call of the Void and the suppression from R Nether Grasp. If Malzahar W Void Swarm’s Voidlings are already out, clear them first.
Malzahar.laning: Keep your distance from minions afflicted by Malzahar E Malefic Visions. When you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, don’t keep pushing the wave with Yone Q Mortal Steel, and save E Soul Unbound. If Malzahar pushes the lane, look for a chance to break P Void Shift and engage with your jungler.
Malzahar.phase: After completing your first core item, break Malzahar P Void Shift and fight aggressively. Malzahar grows stronger as he accumulates more, putting you at a disadvantage over time, so pressure him with your jungler from early on to limit his room to scale.
Malzahar.teamfight: Engage when Malzahar W Void Swarm’s Voidlings are gone or haven’t appeared yet; if they’re already out, clear them first. Activate Yone E Soul Unbound and go in, then hit multiple enemies with W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Use Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team, and don’t go deep alone if Malzahar can use R Nether Grasp.
Malzahar.watch: When a minion afflicted by Malzahar E Malefic Visions dies, the effect jumps to a nearby enemy, so don’t wait beside that minion to last-hit. When you see Malzahar Q Call of the Void, move outside the line between its portals and don’t engage until the silence ends. Malzahar R Nether Grasp’s suppression cannot be removed by Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield or Yone E Soul Unbound’s return.

Irelia.fight: Don’t engage first where Irelia can close in by dashing through minions. Once Irelia Q Bladesurge’s chain of dashes ends and Irelia E Flawless Duet is down, knock her up with your prepared Yone Q Mortal Steel tornado for a short trade. Use Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield to absorb her key ability.
Irelia.build: Prioritize completing your first core item with attack speed and critical strike. If healing from Irelia Q Bladesurge could turn the duel, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder. The available information does not indicate which resistance to build.
Irelia.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare your tornado. After Irelia E Flawless Duet is down, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, engage with tornado Q, then deal damage in this order: basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack. After dealing damage, recast E to return to your original position.
Irelia.escape: The moment after making Irelia use Q Bladesurge is an opportunity to close the distance. However, she can chain Q through minions, so look to engage once that movement ends. Engage with Yone Q Mortal Steel or Yone E Soul Unbound once Irelia E Flawless Duet’s stun is also down.
Irelia.phase: Yone can take the initiative in fights once he completes his first core item with attack speed and critical strike. The available information does not indicate which side is stronger after that.
Irelia.teamfight: Prioritize Irelia before she can use Irelia R Vanguard’s Edge and Irelia E Flawless Duet on your allies. When diving deep, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, then hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build its shield. Use Yone R Fate Sealed to pull Irelia toward your team, and hold it if the path would leave you deep in their formation.
Irelia.watch: Irelia Q Bladesurge can chain through low-health minions to close the distance and heal, so keep away when minions are about to die. While Irelia E Flawless Duet’s stun is available, don’t dive in first with Yone Q Mortal Steel’s tornado or Yone E Soul Unbound. If trapped inside Irelia R Vanguard’s Edge, wait for the blades to disappear.

Ahri.laning: Move with a line of minions between you and Ahri to block Ahri E Charm. When you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, don’t push the wave too far by farming with Q; keep Yone E Soul Unbound available.
Ahri.build: Yone’s power rises greatly once his first core item grants attack speed and critical strike, so prioritize completing it. Consider magic resistance against the magic damage from Ahri Q Orb of Deception and W Fox-Fire, but dodging Charm comes first. If healing from Ahri P Essence Theft can turn a duel around, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Ahri.combo: If Ahri E Charm is down, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first and engage with your prepared charged Yone Q Mortal Steel. Deal damage in this order: basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack, then recast E to return. Check that R will pull Ahri toward your team before using it.
Ahri.escape: If Ahri E Charm has also just been used, close the gap with Yone Q Mortal Steel and Yone E Soul Unbound. Don’t dive in with E where Charm is still available.
Ahri.fight: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a charged Q, but don’t engage first with charged Q while Ahri E Charm is available. After dodging Charm, knock Ahri up with charged Q, land two basic attacks and Yone W Spirit Cleave, then back off. Time W to shield yourself when Ahri’s key damage comes in.
Ahri.phase: Yone can fight proactively after completing his first core item, but check whether Ahri E Charm and R Spirit Rush are available before engaging. The available information isn’t enough to determine who has the advantage late game.
Ahri.teamfight: Use Yone E Soul Unbound to engage on the enemy back line, then hit multiple champions with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Use Yone R Fate Sealed in a direction that pulls enemies toward your team, and save it if its path would carry you through enemies and leave you deep in their team.
Ahri.watch: If Ahri E Charm hits you, you may take the full follow-up, so dodge it with minions between you and Ahri. Ahri Q Orb of Deception can hit you on its return, so even after dodging the first pass, move outside its return path. Magic resistance cannot reduce the true damage on its return.

Camille.phase: Yone becomes much stronger in fights from his first core item, but don’t leave Camille’s split push and tower pressure unchecked from the midgame onward. The given information isn’t enough to determine who has the advantage late game.
Camille.build: Yone’s power rises sharply with his first core item, which provides attack speed and critical strike, so play around that completion timing. Build armor first against Camille’s main damage, but armor cannot reduce the true damage from Camille Q Precision Protocol. If Camille W Tactical Sweep’s healing can turn a duel, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Camille.combo: Before trading, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. For a short trade after Camille E Hookshot is down, knock her up with tornado Q, then hit two basic attacks, Yone W Spirit Cleave, and another basic attack before backing off. For an all-in, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, then use tornado Q, basic attack, W, Yone R Fate Sealed, and basic attack before returning with E.
Camille.escape: After Camille E Hookshot’s wall jump and stun are down, look for a chance to engage with Yone Q Mortal Steel. If Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum is also down, she has no mobility available, so close the gap with Yone E Soul Unbound and Q. If Camille E Hookshot is available, don’t dive deep with Yone E Soul Unbound.
Camille.fight: Avoid trading right after Camille P Adaptive Defenses activates its shield; engage once the shield has been removed. Don’t engage first with tornado from Yone Q Mortal Steel while Camille E Hookshot is available. During the window when Camille E Hookshot and R The Hextech Ultimatum are down, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first and engage while recording damage.
Camille.laning: Stand away from walls. When you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, don’t keep pushing the lane with Q, and save Yone E Soul Unbound. If Camille pushes the lane, a tornado Q angle opens, and Hookshot is down, take a short trade.
Camille.teamfight: With Yone E Soul Unbound active, pressure the backline and secure a place to return to. Hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, and make sure Yone R Fate Sealed’s path pulls Camille toward your team. Don’t waste crowd control when Camille engages with her ultimate, and avoid an R angle that leaves you deep in the enemy team.
Camille.watch: Camille E Hookshot can stun you from far away by starting from a wall, so don’t get cornered near one. When Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum engages, don’t use your counter ability; if trapped, hold out until the zone disappears.

Annie.build: Yone should aim to complete his first core item with attack speed and critical strike. Build magic resistance to withstand Annie’s magic damage, but don’t rely on resistance alone to survive Annie R Summon: Tibbers, which has magic penetration; avoid its stun.
Annie.watch: When Annie P Pyromania is ready to stun, white light swirls around her. Don’t enter ability range then, and don’t stand stacked with allies where Annie R Summon: Tibbers can stun multiple targets.
Annie.combo: Deal damage with a basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack, then recast E to return.
Annie.escape: The opening to engage comes after Annie P Pyromania’s stun is down. Annie can’t use a mobility ability to create distance, so close the gap then with charged Yone Q Mortal Steel.
Annie.fight: Time Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield for Annie’s incoming key abilities, then back off after you’ve landed your basic attacks.
Annie.laning: If you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, don’t keep pushing the wave with Q; keep Yone E Soul Unbound available.
Annie.phase: Once Yone completes his first core item with attack speed and critical strike, fight proactively when Annie’s stun is down. The available information isn’t enough to determine who has the advantage late game.
Annie.teamfight: If Annie is out of sight or Annie P Pyromania’s stun is ready, don’t stand stacked with allies. Engage with Yone E Soul Unbound active and hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Use Yone R Fate Sealed in a direction that can pull Annie toward your team, and save it if its path would leave you deep in their team.

Aatrox.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a charged Q, then activate E Soul Unbound first when Aatrox’s mobility and crowd control are down. Engage with charged Q Mortal Steel to knock him up, then deal damage with basic attacks, W Spirit Cleave, R Fate Sealed, and a basic attack before recasting E Soul Unbound to return. When following up on an ally’s immobilizing effect, knock Aatrox up first with R Fate Sealed and save charged Q Mortal Steel to limit his chance to use E Umbral Dash.
Aatrox.laning: Repeatedly using Yone Q Mortal Steel pushes the lane, so when you don't know where the enemy jungler is, use it sparingly to pull the lane toward you and save Yone E Soul Unbound. If you avoid giving up an early kill and keep up in CS, the matchup improves as the game goes on.
Aatrox.build: Aatrox’s main abilities, Q The Darkin Blade and W Infernal Chains, deal physical damage, so build armor first. Attack speed and critical strike greatly improve Yone’s trading, so look to fight proactively when you complete your first core item. If Aatrox’s healing can turn a long duel around, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Aatrox.escape: Immediately after you make Aatrox use E Umbral Dash, you have an opportunity to close the gap with Yone Q Mortal Steel or E Soul Unbound. Don’t dive in with E Soul Unbound while Aatrox still has the knock-up from Q The Darkin Blade or the pull from W Infernal Chains.
Aatrox.fight: Trade just after Aatrox uses his empowered basic attack from P Deathbringer Stance on a minion or uses E Umbral Dash. Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a charged Q, but don’t engage first with charged Q Mortal Steel or E Soul Unbound while Aatrox still has his knock-up and pull. When Aatrox Q The Darkin Blade comes in, avoid the blade’s edge and time Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield to absorb it.
Aatrox.phase: Once you complete your first core item with attack speed and critical strike, you can fight proactively. If you avoided early losses, the matchup against Aatrox improves as the game goes on.
Aatrox.teamfight: Use Yone E Soul Unbound to pressure the enemy back line, then return safely. Hit multiple enemies with W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, and use R Fate Sealed in a direction that pulls enemies toward your team. Save R Fate Sealed if its path would carry you through several enemies and leave you deep in their team.
Aatrox.watch: Aatrox Q The Darkin Blade deals his main damage and knocks you up, so when you see him cast it, move outside the blade’s edge or move inward past it. If Aatrox W Infernal Chains hits you, leave the area immediately. Save Yone E Soul Unbound or charged Q Mortal Steel for this moment. When Aatrox R World Ender is active, his attack damage and healing increase, so don’t fight him; create distance.

Nasus.watch: Nasus W Wither reduces your movement and attack speed, making it harder for Yone to trade with basic attacks, so don't fight for long while affected. Nasus E Spirit Fire reduces your armor while you're standing on it, so move out of the area. When Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active, stop fighting and let it run out.
Nasus.build: Prioritize armor against Nasus Q Siphoning Strike, his main source of damage. Nasus E Spirit Fire and R Fury of the Sands deal magic damage, so armor alone won’t block everything. Yone gets stronger with attack speed and critical strike chance, so take the initiative once you have them.
Nasus.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, then knock Nasus up with tornado Q and trade briefly with two basic attacks → Yone W Spirit Cleave → basic attack. For an all-in, first activate Yone E Soul Unbound, then deal damage with tornado Q → basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack before recasting E to return. Time Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield to absorb Nasus’s key damage.
Nasus.escape: After Nasus uses W Wither is a good opening for Yone to engage. Nasus has no way to create distance on his own other than Flash, so you can close in with Yone Q Mortal Steel’s tornado and Yone E Soul Unbound. Don’t go deep with Yone E Soul Unbound while Nasus W Wither is available.
Nasus.fight: Then hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, and make a short engage after Nasus uses W Wither. If Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active, avoid fighting unless you have a clear advantage.
Nasus.laning: If you push Nasus under his turret, it becomes easier for him to stack with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike, so let the wave come to your side. When you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, don’t keep pushing the wave with Yone Q Mortal Steel, and save Yone E Soul Unbound. Pressure Nasus when he comes out to last-hit with Q, and look for a gank from your jungler while the wave is near your side.
Nasus.phase: Yone gets stronger once he has attack speed and critical strike chance, while Nasus grows stronger as he stacks, so limit his chances to scale from early on.
Nasus.teamfight: Don’t fight Nasus head-on while Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active; keep your distance. Activate Yone E Soul Unbound to engage, hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, then return. Use Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team, and hold it if the angle would leave you deep in their formation.

Orianna.phase: After completing his first core item with attack speed and critical strike, Yone can take the initiative in fights. There isn't enough information to say who has the advantage late game, so in teamfights, prioritize an angle that lets you get back out alive after engaging.
Orianna.build: Prioritize attack speed and critical strike chance to take advantage of your power spike when you complete your first core item. If you need to withstand Orianna’s attacks, build magic resistance. Use movement speed to get out of the area telegraphed by Orianna Q Command: Attack.
Orianna.combo: For a trade, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. After Orianna Q Command: Attack moves the ball away from her, deal damage with tornado Q → two basic attacks → Yone W Spirit Cleave → basic attack. For an all-in, first activate Yone E Soul Unbound, then deal damage with tornado Q → basic attack → W → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack before returning with E.
Orianna.escape: Engage after Orianna Q Command: Attack moves the ball away from her and you have a safe position from which to dodge Orianna R Command: Shockwave. If you’re caught by Orianna’s strong crowd control, you cannot return with Yone E Soul Unbound, so don’t dive deep near the ball.
Orianna.fight: Right after Orianna Q Command: Attack moves the ball away from her, she lacks the persistent defensive stats from Orianna E Command: Protect, so look to trade. Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, then engage briefly, and don’t take Orianna’s repeated basic attacks for long.
Orianna.laning: When you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, don’t keep pushing the lane with Q, and save Yone E Soul Unbound. If Orianna has pushed the lane and thrown the ball, look for a chance to engage with a tornado.
Orianna.teamfight: Activate Yone E Soul Unbound and dive into the backline, then hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Use Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team, and avoid angles that carry you through several enemies and leave you deep in their formation. Judge the threat from Orianna R Command: Shockwave by the ball’s position, not Orianna’s.
Orianna.watch: Watch where Orianna Q Command: Attack places the ball and move accordingly. Near the ball, Orianna R Command: Shockwave can pull you in, so don’t stay there. When hit by the slow from Orianna W Command: Dissonance, time Yone W Spirit Cleave to gain a shield.

Riven.build: Yone prioritizes attack speed and critical strike to complete his first core item. Riven's damage is physical, so build armor; if Riven gets ahead, get defensive items sooner. Riven R Blade of the Exile is more dangerous when your health is low, so consider building health as well.
Riven.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare your dash. After Riven Q Broken Wings and Riven W Ki Burst are down, deal damage with Yone E Soul Unbound → dash Q Mortal Steel → basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack, then recast E Soul Unbound to return.
Riven.escape: If only Riven Q Broken Wings is down, Riven can escape with Riven E Valor, so don’t go deep right away. Engage with Yone E Soul Unbound and dash Q Mortal Steel during a window before Riven Q Broken Wings is available again and while Riven W Ki Burst is also down. If Riven’s crowd control is still available, you may be unable to return in time after diving in with E Soul Unbound.
Riven.fight: Look to counterattack after Riven uses Q Broken Wings to clear minions. Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare your dash, confirm Riven W Ki Burst is down, then go in briefly and trade with basic attacks and Yone W Spirit Cleave. Time Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield for when Riven’s key damage comes in.
Riven.laning: Repeatedly using Q pushes the lane, so if you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, use it less to let the lane come toward you and save Yone E Soul Unbound. Look to trade when Riven pushes the lane or uses Riven Q Broken Wings on minions.
Riven.phase: After completing your first core item, use your attack speed and critical strike to take the initiative when Riven Q Broken Wings is down. The available information is not enough to determine who has the advantage late game.
Riven.teamfight: With Yone E Soul Unbound active, get behind the enemy team and hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build your shield. Use Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies, including Riven, toward your team, and avoid angles that pass through enemies and land you deep in their team. If Riven Q Broken Wings and Riven W Ki Burst are available, account for them disrupting follow-up with Yone Q Mortal Steel or R Fate Sealed.
Riven.watch: Riven Q Broken Wings closes the gap with repeated dashes and a knock-up, and Riven W Ki Burst can interrupt Yone Q Mortal Steel’s cast. When Riven uses her first dash, back away. While Riven R Blade of the Exile is active, keep your distance, accounting for the increased range and damage that scales with missing health.

Sett.build: Yone prioritizes attack speed and critical strike to use the power spike when he completes his first core item. Build armor first for resistance against Sett P Pit Grit and Sett Q Knuckle Down. Resistance can't reduce the true damage at the center of Sett W Haymaker, and Sett Q Knuckle Down deals damage based on your maximum health, so don't rely on stacking health alone.
Sett.combo: Before trading, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare the tornado. In a short trade after Sett E Facebreaker is down, knock him up with tornado Q, then use two basic attacks, Yone W Spirit Cleave, and a basic attack before backing off. For an all-in, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, then use tornado Q, a basic attack, W, Yone R Fate Sealed, and a basic attack, then recast E to return.
Sett.escape: Once you confirm Sett E Facebreaker is down too, close the gap with Yone Q Mortal Steel’s tornado and Yone E Soul Unbound. If Sett still has an immobilizing ability available, don’t go deep with E; keep a path open for your return.
Sett.fight: Don’t engage first with Yone Q Mortal Steel’s tornado while Sett E Facebreaker is available. After dealing damage, back off at the moment Sett W Haymaker grows stronger, then re-engage.
Sett.laning: Repeatedly using Q will push the wave, so when you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, use it less to pull the lane toward you and save Yone E Soul Unbound. If Sett has pushed the lane, look for an angle to engage with tornado Q.
Sett.phase: Once you have attack speed and critical strike chance and complete your first core item, Yone can take the initiative in fights. The information provided isn’t enough to determine who has the edge late game, so prioritize engages you can survive and return from in teamfights.
Sett.teamfight: Use Yone E Soul Unbound to pressure the enemy backline and return. Hit multiple champions with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build its shield, and aim Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team. Avoid angles where R passes through several enemies and leaves you deep in their team, and don’t stand where enemies on both sides of Sett would allow his E Facebreaker to stun you.
Sett.watch: Sett W Haymaker becomes dangerous right after Sett takes a lot of damage. Use Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield to absorb key damage, and when Sett W Haymaker comes out, sidestep the center of its indicator to avoid the true damage. Sett E Facebreaker stuns if there are enemies on both sides of Sett, so don’t get caught between Sett and a minion wave.

Tryndamere.build: Tryndamere's main damage is physical, so build armor first. Once Yone has attack speed and critical strike, he's better positioned to take the initiative in fights. If Tryndamere Q Bloodlust heals enough to turn the duel, buy Executioner's Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Tryndamere.combo: Once Tryndamere E Spinning Slash is down, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, then engage with your prepared tornado, Yone Q Mortal Steel. Deal damage in this order: basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack. Then recast Yone E Soul Unbound to return. When Tryndamere R Undying Rage is active, don't keep unloading the combo; spend its duration knocking him up and returning.
Tryndamere.escape: The moment after you bait out Tryndamere E Spinning Slash is your chance to engage with Yone Q Mortal Steel and Yone E Soul Unbound. Avoid trading basic attacks right after being hit by Tryndamere W Mocking Shout. After Tryndamere E Spinning Slash is down, landing the knockup from Yone Q Mortal Steel or Yone R Fate Sealed can limit his chance to create distance again.
Tryndamere.fight: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, then make a short trade after Tryndamere E Spinning Slash is down. Knock him up with Yone Q Mortal Steel, land two basic attacks and Yone W Spirit Cleave, then retreat. When Tryndamere R Undying Rage is active, let it run out with knockups and distance instead of unloading your attacks.
Tryndamere.laning: Harassing Tryndamere to deny last hits can suppress both his Fury and healing from Tryndamere Q Bloodlust. When you don't know where the enemy jungler is, don't keep pushing the wave with Yone Q Mortal Steel; pull the lane toward you and save Yone E Soul Unbound.
Tryndamere.phase: Take the initiative in fights once you've completed your first core item and have attack speed and critical strike. Even later, if Tryndamere R Undying Rage is ready, don't try to hold him alone in a side lane; check whether he uses R or send more players.
Tryndamere.teamfight: Activate Yone E Soul Unbound and get behind the enemy, while keeping in mind where you'll return. Hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, and use Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your allies. If Tryndamere R Undying Rage is active, knock him up with Yone Q Mortal Steel or Yone R Fate Sealed and let it run out instead of unloading your damage.
Tryndamere.watch: When Tryndamere P Battle Fury is stacked, his critical strikes become dangerous, and Tryndamere Q Bloodlust heals more, so keep your distance while he builds Fury by hitting minions. If hit by Tryndamere W Mocking Shout, avoid trading basic attacks while your attack damage is reduced; when retreating, walk backward while facing Tryndamere. When Tryndamere R Undying Rage is active, don't keep dealing damage. Knock him up with Yone Q Mortal Steel or Yone R Fate Sealed, or create distance and let it run out.

Urgot.build: Urgot P Echoing Flames, Urgot Q Corrosive Charge, and Urgot W Purge deal mostly physical damage, so build armor first. Yone can take the initiative in fights from the point he completes his first core item with attack speed and critical strike.
Urgot.fight: The moment after you bait out Urgot E Disdain is Yone's chance to close the distance. Before fighting, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado; once you're in, land two basic attacks and Yone W Spirit Cleave, then retreat. Don't stay near Urgot for long, so his leg-gun damage doesn't stack up.
Urgot.watch: Urgot P Echoing Flames deals damage based on maximum health, so don't stay near Urgot for long. If hit by Urgot Q Corrosive Charge, its strong slow lets Urgot W Purge focus its fire on you, so decide whether to escape with Yone Q Mortal Steel or Yone E Soul Unbound as the projectile comes in. Don't engage first with tornado Q while Urgot E Disdain is ready. If hit by Urgot R Fear Beyond Death, get completely out of range before reaching the execute threshold.
Urgot.combo: Once Urgot E Disdain is down, cast Yone E Soul Unbound first, then engage with a Yone Q Mortal Steel tornado you prepared earlier. Deal damage with basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack, then recast Yone E Soul Unbound to return. If following up on an ally’s immobilize, use Yone R Fate Sealed first and save tornado Q to reduce Urgot’s chance to escape with Urgot E Disdain.
Urgot.escape: Engage right after Urgot E Disdain, his only mobility ability, is down. While Urgot E Disdain is available, don’t dive in first with Yone Q Mortal Steel’s tornado or Yone E Soul Unbound. If Urgot Q Corrosive Charge hits and makes it hard to escape on foot, decide immediately whether to get out with Yone Q Mortal Steel, Yone E Soul Unbound, or Yone R Fate Sealed.
Urgot.laning: Melee champions have a hard time beating Urgot head-on in lane, so choose farming over a forced fight, or take him down together with your jungler. When you don't know where the enemy jungler is, manage your Q farming to avoid pushing the lane and save Yone E Soul Unbound.
Urgot.phase: Yone can take the initiative in fights from the point when his first core item gives him attack speed and critical strike. Late game, play around engaging with Yone E Soul Unbound, dealing damage, and returning instead of staying near Urgot for long.
Urgot.teamfight: Aim to pressure the backline and get back out alive while Yone E Soul Unbound is active. Hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, and use Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team. Urgot E Disdain stops at the first champion it hits, so having your frontline in front can reduce the risk to allies behind them.

Akali.build: Prioritize magic resistance over armor to withstand Akali’s damage, and build enough health to survive the second hit of Akali R Perfect Execution.
Akali.combo: Build stacks of Yone Q Mortal Steel on minions, then for a short trade knock Akali up with charged Q and follow with two basic attacks, Yone W Spirit Cleave, and a basic attack. For an all-in, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, then use charged Q, a basic attack, Yone W Spirit Cleave, Yone R Fate Sealed, and a basic attack before returning with E. When following up on an ally’s immobilizing effect, use Yone R Fate Sealed first and save charged Q to limit Akali’s chance to use her mobility.
Akali.escape: You can close the gap with Yone Q Mortal Steel, Yone E Soul Unbound, and Yone R Fate Sealed if Akali R Perfect Execution is also still on cooldown. If only one of her mobility options is down, don’t dive in recklessly because Akali still has another way to escape.
Akali.fight: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a charged Q, then fight back when Akali comes out of W Twilight Shroud to attack. Use Yone W Spirit Cleave to shield yourself when Akali’s key damage comes in, then back off once you’ve dealt your damage.
Akali.laning: Repeated Q use pushes the wave, so when you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, farm with Q less to pull the wave toward you and keep Yone E Soul Unbound available. If Akali has pushed the wave, use your prepared charged Q to close in and look for a trade.
Akali.teamfight: Use Yone E Soul Unbound to pressure the back line and secure a place to return to. Hit multiple champions with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, and use Yone R Fate Sealed in a direction that pulls enemies toward your team. Save your ultimate if its path would carry you through several enemies and leave you deep in their team.
Akali.watch: If a mark is applied to you, a second dash will follow, so if you’ve been hit, time Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield for when the damage comes in.

Akshan.build: Prioritize armor against the main damage from Akshan Q Avengerang, E Heroic Swing, and R Comeuppance. After that, build attack speed and critical strike to increase Yone’s fighting power from his first core item onward.
Akshan.combo: When Akshan E Heroic Swing is down, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, then engage with your prepared charged Yone Q Mortal Steel. Deal damage with a basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack, then recast Yone E Soul Unbound to return.
Akshan.escape: Immediately after you make Akshan use E Heroic Swing, you have an opportunity to close the gap. Engage then with the tornado from Yone Q Mortal Steel or Yone E Soul Unbound, and check that Yone R Fate Sealed will pull Akshan toward your team before using it.
Akshan.fight: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a charged Q, and engage when Akshan E Heroic Swing is down. Knock him up with Yone Q Mortal Steel, land two basic attacks and Yone W Spirit Cleave, then back off. Time Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield for when Akshan’s attacks hit you.
Akshan.laning: Don’t rely on standing behind minions to dodge Akshan Q Avengerang; watch its path in both directions. When you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, manage Yone Q Mortal Steel so you don’t push the wave, and keep Yone E Soul Unbound available.
Akshan.phase: Once Yone completes his first core item with attack speed and critical strike, fight proactively when Akshan E Heroic Swing is down. Late game, fight from angles that let Yone E Soul Unbound return you safely rather than assuming either champion is stronger.
Akshan.watch: Akshan Q Avengerang gains range with each enemy it hits, so even behind minions, dodge both its outgoing and return paths. Akshan R Comeuppance is more dangerous when you’ve lost more health, so when your health is low, get behind terrain to block the shots.
Akshan.teamfight: If a Scoundrel mark is applied after an allied unit is killed, don’t face Akshan alone; fight outside his finishing range. Activate Yone E Soul Unbound to engage and hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Use Yone R Fate Sealed in a direction that pulls enemies toward your team, and save it if its path would leave you deep in their team.

Ambessa.build: Prioritize completing your first core item with attack speed and critical strike. Ambessa’s main damage is physical, so choose armor if you build resistance. If Ambessa’s healing can turn a duel around, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Ambessa.combo: Wait until Ambessa W Repudiation finishes its windup and her immobilizing abilities are down, then build stacks of Yone Q Mortal Steel on minions. For a short trade, knock her up with charged Q, follow with two basic attacks, Yone W Spirit Cleave, and a basic attack, then back off. For an all-in, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, then deal damage with charged Q, a basic attack, W, Yone R Fate Sealed, and a basic attack before recasting E to return.
Ambessa.escape: Engage immediately after Ambessa has spent her abilities and her P Drakehound’s Step charges. If Ambessa E Lacerate hits you, immediately find an angle to dodge the next attack with E.
Ambessa.fight: Trade immediately after Ambessa has spent her abilities and her P Drakehound’s Step charges. Before trading, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a charged Q, and don’t attack during Ambessa W Repudiation’s windup. If Ambessa still has an immobilizing ability available, don’t dive in first with charged Q or Yone E Soul Unbound.
Ambessa.laning: Repeated Q use pushes the wave, so when you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, farm with Q less to pull the wave toward you and keep Yone E Soul Unbound available. If Ambessa pushes the wave and gives you an angle to engage with charged Q, trade only after she has used her abilities.
Ambessa.phase: Yone can fight aggressively from his first core item with attack speed and critical strike, but Ambessa also becomes strong as she builds core items in the mid game.
Ambessa.teamfight: Use Yone E Soul Unbound to pressure the back line and secure a path to return safely. Hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, but don’t attack during Ambessa W Repudiation’s windup. Use Yone R Fate Sealed in a direction that pulls enemies toward your team, and position so your back line isn’t at the end of the straight path of Ambessa R Public Execution.
Ambessa.watch: When you see Ambessa W Repudiation begin to wind up, stop attacking and walk out of its range. If you dodge the first hit of Ambessa Q Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam, the second hit won’t be ready; if it’s hard to dodge, move toward Ambessa rather than the blade’s edge to reduce the damage. If Ambessa E Lacerate hits you, don’t wait for the slow to wear off; use Yone E Soul Unbound to dodge the next Q.

Anivia.build: Anivia’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first. Then build attack speed and critical strike to increase Yone’s power, and look to start fights proactively once you complete your first core item.
Anivia.combo: Before trading, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a charged Q. Once Anivia Q Flash Frost is down, deal damage in this order: Yone E Soul Unbound → charged Yone Q Mortal Steel → basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack, then recast Yone E Soul Unbound to return.
Anivia.escape: Anivia has no mobility, so when Anivia Q Flash Frost is down, you have an opportunity to close the gap. Make sure you have a place to return to when choosing your engage path.
Anivia.fight: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a charged Q, and engage after Anivia Q Flash Frost is down. Activate Yone E Soul Unbound first so you can make full use of its extra damage when you return. If Anivia P Rebirth is still available, engage with an ally who can destroy the egg; if she has already used it, use that opening to look for a kill.
Anivia.laning: Repeatedly using Yone Q Mortal Steel pushes the wave, so when you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, use it less and keep Yone E Soul Unbound available. If Anivia pushes the wave, prepare a charged Q and look for a trade.
Anivia.phase: Late game, account for Anivia’s terrain control and fight in open areas rather than narrow paths.
Anivia.teamfight: In an open area, activate Yone E Soul Unbound, pressure the enemy back line, and return safely. Hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, and use Yone R Fate Sealed in a direction that pulls enemies toward your team. Be cautious about engaging in narrow passages where Anivia W Crystallize could split you from your allies.
Anivia.watch: Anivia Q Flash Frost can be recast to detonate and stun, so don’t engage just because you dodged its initial path. If it hits you, Anivia E Frostbite deals more damage while you’re chilled, so get out of Anivia R Glacial Storm to dodge her next attack. In narrow paths, Anivia W Crystallize can block your escape route.

AurelionSol.build: Build magic resistance first against Aurelion Sol’s main damage. Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid choices that only add a large amount of health.
AurelionSol.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a charged Q. For an all-in, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, knock Aurelion Sol up with charged Q, then deal damage in this order: basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack. Recast E to return. Check that R will pull Aurelion Sol toward your team before using it.
AurelionSol.escape: Immediately after you make Aurelion Sol use W Astral Flight, you have an opportunity to engage. Don’t dive in with Yone E Soul Unbound where Aurelion Sol still has an immobilizing effect available. If you engage, deal your damage and use E to return to your starting position.
AurelionSol.fight: Then hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a charged Q, and close in for a short trade after Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is down. Use Yone W Spirit Cleave to shield yourself when Aurelion Sol’s key attack hits.
AurelionSol.laning: Don’t take unnecessary hits from Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light and give him Stardust; during poke, stand behind minions and move out of its aim line. Repeatedly using Yone Q Mortal Steel pushes the wave, so when you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, farm with Q less to pull the wave toward you and keep Yone E Soul Unbound available. If the enemy has pushed the wave and Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is down, trade with your prepared charged Q.
AurelionSol.phase: Aurelion Sol is weakest early, before he has Stardust, so Yone should look to take advantage of openings after his first core item increases his power and Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is down. Aurelion Sol grows stronger late game with permanently accumulated Stardust, so don’t expect the same engage angles and watch out for his area abilities.
AurelionSol.teamfight: Use Yone E Soul Unbound to pressure the back line, then return safely. Hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, but avoid angles where Yone R Fate Sealed would leave you deep in the enemy team. Keep your distance from allies so several of you aren’t hit together by Aurelion Sol R Falling Star / The Skies Descend when he has built Stardust.
AurelionSol.watch: Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light deals extra damage and builds Stardust if it hits you for a long time, so stand behind minions and quickly move out of its aim line. When your health is low, avoid the center of Aurelion Sol E Singularity, which can execute you, and move outward immediately if you’re caught in it. Once he has built Stardust, keep your distance from allies to avoid Aurelion Sol R Falling Star / The Skies Descend’s area knock-up.

Aurora.build: For your first core item, build attack speed and critical strike to strengthen trades with Yone Q Mortal Steel and your shield use with Yone W Spirit Cleave. Build magic resistance rather than armor against Aurora’s damage. If Aurora P Spirit Abjuration’s healing can turn a duel, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Aurora.combo: Before trading, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. For an all-in, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, knock Aurora up with tornado Q, then deal damage in this order: basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack. Then return with E. Don’t cast recklessly while Aurora W Across the Veil makes her invisible; watch where she reappears.
Aurora.escape: Aurora W Across the Veil, E The Weirding, and R Between Worlds all provide mobility, so don’t all-in just because one is down. In particular, when Aurora R Between Worlds is down and W and E are also down, close the gap with Yone Q Mortal Steel and E Soul Unbound. Before engaging, choose where you’ll return with E.
Aurora.fight: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, then trade when Aurora has pushed the lane. Time Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield to absorb the damage from Aurora Q Twofold Hex, and don’t stay in an extended fight while low on health and cursed. Make Aurora use Aurora E The Weirding to create distance, check for any remaining mobility, then re-engage.
Aurora.laning: Repeated Q casts push the lane, so when you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, use it less, pull the wave, and save Yone E Soul Unbound. If Aurora pushes the lane, look for a chance to close in with tornado Q.
Aurora.phase: Once you have attack speed and critical strike and complete your first core item, take the initiative in trades, but check Aurora’s remaining mobility. The given information isn’t enough to determine who has the advantage late game, so in teamfights prioritize engages that let you return with Yone E Soul Unbound.
Aurora.teamfight: With Yone E Soul Unbound active, engage the backline and hit multiple champions with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Cast Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team, and avoid an angle that carries you through them and leaves you deep in the enemy team. If Aurora uses her leap to engage and doesn’t help secure a kill, look for a chance to catch her. When retreating, don’t leave low-health allies behind.
Aurora.watch: Aurora Q Twofold Hex deals damage again when recalled, and that damage increases the more health the target is missing. If cursed, move out of the line between Aurora and you. If your health is low, back off before the curse is recalled. Before Aurora R Between Worlds appears, decide whether to disengage or fight inside the zone.

Azir.build: Build attack speed first to make use of Yone Q Mortal Steel and reduce Yone W Spirit Cleave’s cast time and cooldown. Then build critical strike. If you need to withstand Azir’s magic damage, build magic resistance rather than armor.
Azir.combo: Prepare tornado with Yone Q Mortal Steel on minions, then activate Yone E Soul Unbound first. Knock Azir up with tornado Q, then deal damage in this order: basic attack, Yone W Spirit Cleave, Yone R Fate Sealed, basic attack. Recast E to return. If Azir E Shifting Sands is available, follow up on an ally’s immobilizing effect with Yone R Fate Sealed, and save tornado Q to limit Azir’s chance to escape.
Azir.escape: Right after Azir uses Azir E Shifting Sands is your chance to close the gap with Yone Q Mortal Steel, E Soul Unbound, and R Fate Sealed. If Azir R Emperor’s Divide is available, it can knock you back, so choose your engage angle carefully. When you go in with Yone E Soul Unbound, also check where you’ll return.
Azir.fight: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, then approach from the side while Azir’s soldiers are stationary. If you make Azir use Azir E Shifting Sands, engage with Yone E Soul Unbound, deal a quick burst of damage, and return.
Azir.laning: If repeated Q casts push the lane and Yone E Soul Unbound is also down, you become vulnerable to ganks. When you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, let the wave come toward you and save E.
Azir.phase: After completing your first core item, use Yone’s attack speed and critical strike to take the initiative in short trades. Azir grows stronger as the game goes on, so late game don’t spend a long time facing his soldiers; focus your damage when you have a chance to catch him.
Azir.teamfight: With Yone E Soul Unbound active, get into the backline and clip multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Cast Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team, and avoid an angle that carries you through several enemies and leaves you deep in their team. Azir R Emperor’s Divide can knock several enemies back, so don’t engage together in a narrow passage.
Azir.watch: Standing in the line of Azir W Arise! soldiers leaves you taking continuous damage, so circle around to approach Azir himself. Watch for Azir Q Conquering Sands to move his soldiers or slow you, and don’t force an engage in a narrow passage while Azir R Emperor’s Divide is available.

Cassiopeia.build: All of Cassiopeia’s damage skills deal magic damage, so build magic resistance if you need resistance. If Cassiopeia E Twin Fang’s healing can turn a duel, slot Executioner’s Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Cassiopeia.combo: Before trading, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. For a safe short trade, knock Cassiopeia up with tornado Q, then use two basic attacks, Yone W Spirit Cleave, and another basic attack before backing off. For an all-in when Cassiopeia W Miasma and R Petrifying Gaze no longer pose a threat to your engage, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, then use tornado Q, basic attack, W, Yone R Fate Sealed, and basic attack before recasting E to return.
Cassiopeia.escape: Cassiopeia has no mobility, so right after she uses Cassiopeia W Miasma elsewhere is your chance to close the gap. If W is down on the ground, approach along a path that avoids the cloud, and don’t dive deep with Yone E Soul Unbound while Cassiopeia R Petrifying Gaze is available. If Cassiopeia Q Noxious Blast hits you, re-engage after the poison ends.
Cassiopeia.fight: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, then take short trades along a path not covered by Cassiopeia W Miasma. If Cassiopeia Q Noxious Blast hits you, back off until the poison ends, and don’t face her for long while Cassiopeia R Petrifying Gaze is available. Use Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield when Cassiopeia’s key skill is about to hit.
Cassiopeia.laning: When you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, don’t keep pushing the wave with Yone Q Mortal Steel; pull the lane and save Yone E Soul Unbound.
Cassiopeia.phase: Yone can take the initiative from his first core item, but late-game Cassiopeia can win teamfights with sustained damage if she isn’t caught, so choose your engage timing carefully.
Cassiopeia.teamfight: Take control of vision to cut off Cassiopeia’s path or engage right after she uses Cassiopeia W Miasma elsewhere, instead of pushing straight at her. With Yone E Soul Unbound active, knock her up first with Yone Q Mortal Steel or Yone R Fate Sealed, then hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Cast R to pull enemies toward your team, and avoid a path that leaves you deep in the enemy team.
Cassiopeia.watch: If Cassiopeia Q Noxious Blast hits you, Cassiopeia E Twin Fang deals more damage and heals more while you’re poisoned, so move out of range and re-engage when the poison ends. You can’t use movement skills like Yone Q Mortal Steel and Yone E Soul Unbound inside Cassiopeia W Miasma, so go around the cloud. When you see Cassiopeia R Petrifying Gaze’s cast animation, turn away to avoid the stun.

Chogath.build: Prioritize completing your first core item with attack speed and critical strike to improve Yone’s trading. Magic resistance is more effective than armor against Cho'Gath Q Rupture, W Feral Scream, and E Vorpal Spikes, but resistance cannot block the true damage from Cho'Gath R Feast. If Cho'Gath P Carnivore’s healing can turn a duel, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Chogath.combo: If Cho'Gath Q Rupture and W Feral Scream are down, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first. Knock him up with the prepared tornado from Yone Q Mortal Steel, then deal damage in this order: basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack. Recast E to return. For a short trade, use only tornado Q → two basic attacks → W → basic attack, then back off.
Chogath.escape: When Cho'Gath Q Rupture’s knock-up and W Feral Scream’s silence are down, engage with Yone Q Mortal Steel’s tornado or Yone E Soul Unbound. Don’t dive deep with Yone E Soul Unbound while both skills are available.
Chogath.fight: Before trading, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. After Cho'Gath Q Rupture or W Feral Scream is down, engage with tornado Q and land two basic attacks at a time, using Yone W Spirit Cleave to absorb his counterattack. Since Cho'Gath has no mobility skill to create distance, repeat short trades when you have a safe engage angle to pressure him.
Chogath.laning: Stand to the side of Cho'Gath’s basic attack direction so Cho'Gath E Vorpal Spikes doesn’t hit you along with the minions. When you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, don’t keep pushing the wave with Q; save Yone E Soul Unbound, and pressure Cho'Gath after he uses Cho'Gath Q Rupture on the wave.
Chogath.phase: Cho'Gath becomes tankier as his Feast stacks increase, making him harder to deal with over time, so pressure him when Yone gets stronger to slow his growth. Late game, don’t give him a kill by staying within Cho'Gath R Feast range at uncertain health.
Chogath.teamfight: Engage with Yone E Soul Unbound active and hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Cast Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team, and hold it if the angle would carry you through several enemies and leave you deep in their team. If Cho'Gath Q Rupture and W Feral Scream are available, account for your return path when engaging, then return with E after dealing damage.
Chogath.watch: Cho'Gath Q Rupture has a ground indicator, so immediately move to the side and save Yone E Soul Unbound or Yone Q Mortal Steel’s dash to dodge it. If Cho'Gath W Feral Scream silences you, you can’t use mobility skills, so avoid facing him head-on; if hit, walk away first. If your health is at half or lower, create distance to stay safe from the true damage of Cho'Gath R Feast.

Corki.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Corki E Gatling Gun and R Missile Barrage. Resistance doesn’t affect the true damage from Corki P Hextech Munitions, so also consider your total health.
Corki.combo: After seeing Corki W Valkyrie go down, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first. Engage with the prepared tornado from Yone Q Mortal Steel and knock him up, then deal damage in this order: basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack. Then recast Yone E Soul Unbound to return to your starting position.
Corki.escape: Corki W Valkyrie is his only mobility skill, so right after he uses it is your chance to close the gap with Yone Q Mortal Steel, Yone E Soul Unbound, and Yone R Fate Sealed. When Corki W Valkyrie is available, he can escape over terrain, so don’t dive too deep.
Corki.fight: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, then engage when Corki W Valkyrie is down. For a short trade, knock him up with tornado, land two basic attacks, then use Yone W Spirit Cleave to gain a shield as Corki’s damage comes in. Move to the side to avoid taking Corki E Gatling Gun head-on for long, then end the trade.
Corki.laning: Then, if Corki has pushed the lane and used Corki W Valkyrie, close in with tornado to pressure his early farming. When you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, don’t keep pushing the lane with Yone Q Mortal Steel; save Yone E Soul Unbound.
Corki.phase: Corki also has low base stats during the first five levels, so pressure his farming during that window when Corki W Valkyrie is down. Yone can take the initiative after completing his first core item; don’t give Corki time to farm comfortably while building items. In the mid and late game, Corki can fire Corki R Missile Barrage from a safe position, so reposition to avoid taking multiple hits in a row.
Corki.teamfight: With Yone E Soul Unbound active, target Corki in the backline and engage when Corki W Valkyrie is down. Hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Cast Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team, and hold it if the path would leave you deep in the enemy team.
Corki.watch: Corki R Missile Barrage also damages targets around the first one hit, so don’t hide behind minions; move out of range. In particular, reposition so you don’t get hit by the third missile in quick succession. Corki E Gatling Gun reduces both armor and magic resistance, so don’t stand and tank it head-on; move to the side. If Corki Q Phosphorus Bomb reveals your position while you’re retreating, immediately create distance with a mobility skill like Yone E Soul Unbound.

Darius.build: Yone’s trading power rises sharply with attack speed and critical strike, so aim to complete your first core item. Build armor first against Darius’s physical damage, but account for the fact that armor cannot block the true damage from Darius R Noxian Guillotine. If Darius Q Decimate’s healing can turn a duel, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Darius.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. Once Darius E Apprehend is down, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first. Knock him up with tornado Q, then deal damage in this order: basic attack, Yone W Spirit Cleave, Yone R Fate Sealed, basic attack. Recast E to return.
Darius.escape: Engage while Darius E Apprehend is down, either because it missed or is on cooldown. While Darius R Noxian Guillotine is down is also a chance to close the gap with Yone Q Mortal Steel, Yone E Soul Unbound, and Yone R Fate Sealed. When E Apprehend is available, don’t engage first with tornado Q or dive deep with E Soul Unbound.
Darius.fight: After Darius E Apprehend is down, hit a minion with Yone Q Mortal Steel and use the prepared tornado for a short engage. You can also poke right after Darius uses Darius Q Decimate to clear minions. End the trade before Darius P Hemorrhage stacks build; if they start stacking, back off and break contact.
Darius.laning: Repeated Q casts push the wave, so when you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, use Q to farm less, pull the lane, and save Yone E Soul Unbound. If Darius pushes the lane and Darius E Apprehend is down, take a short trade with tornado Q.
Darius.phase: Afterward, too, watch out for the healing from Darius Q Decimate and maximum stacks of Darius P Hemorrhage in extended fights; hit briefly and back off.
Darius.teamfight: With Yone E Soul Unbound active, pressure the enemy backline and return alive. Use Yone W Spirit Cleave to clip multiple enemies and build a larger shield, and cast Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team. If you remain in the fight with several stacks of Darius P Hemorrhage and die to Darius R Noxian Guillotine, he can recast his ultimate, so get out of range.
Darius.watch: If Darius E Apprehend pulls you in, he can follow with basic attacks, Darius W Crippling Strike, and Darius Q Decimate, so poke from outside E range. When you see Darius Q Decimate, move out of the axe’s outer edge or hug him closely to reduce its damage and healing. Create distance while Darius P Hemorrhage stacks build, and if you’re low with several stacks, move fully out of Darius R Noxian Guillotine range.

Diana.build: Yone should complete his first core item with attack speed and critical strike first to improve his trading. Diana’s main damage is magic damage, so choose magic resistance if you need resistance.
Diana.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. Once Diana W Pale Cascade is down, knock her up with tornado Q, then trade in this order: two basic attacks → Yone W Spirit Cleave → basic attack. For an all-in, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, then deal damage with tornado Q → basic attack → W → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack before recasting E to return.
Diana.escape: If Diana Q Crescent Strike marks you, Diana E Lunar Rush may reset, so don’t engage; create distance. Right after Diana uses E without a mark, her mobility is down and you can close in with Yone Q Mortal Steel. Don’t dive deep with Yone E Soul Unbound while Diana R Moonfall is available.
Diana.fight: Then hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, and take a short trade after Diana W Pale Cascade’s orbs and shield disappear. If Diana engages first with E Lunar Rush without a mark, counterattack during the window while that mobility skill is down.
Diana.laning: Repeated casts of Yone Q Mortal Steel push the lane, so when you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, use it less and save Yone E Soul Unbound.
Diana.phase: Take the initiative in fights with Yone from the moment you complete your first core item with attack speed and critical strike.
Diana.teamfight: Spread out from your allies and look for a flank so multiple champions aren’t pulled in together by Diana R Moonfall. With Yone E Soul Unbound active, pressure the backline and hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Cast Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team, and hold it if the angle would leave you deep in the enemy team.
Diana.watch: Diana Q Crescent Strike curves as it flies, so sidestep it. If it hits and marks you, Diana E Lunar Rush may reset, so create distance. Don’t engage right after Diana W Pale Cascade activates; wait for its orbs and shield to disappear.

DrMundo.build: Build armor first against Dr. Mundo E Blunt Force Trauma. If his healing can turn the duel, buy Executioner's Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder. Yone becomes strong in fights once he has attack speed and critical strike items.
DrMundo.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, then activate Yone E Soul Unbound first. Use tornado Q to remove Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases, then deal damage with basic attacks and Yone W Spirit Cleave before knocking him up with Yone R Fate Sealed and adding another basic attack. After dealing damage, recast E to return to your starting position.
DrMundo.escape: Once Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases is down, you have an opportunity to use the knock-ups from Yone Q Mortal Steel and Yone R Fate Sealed. Dr. Mundo has no ability to create distance on his own, so use Yone E Soul Unbound to close the gap, but calculate your return position and timing before going in. If Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is active, don’t spend time chasing him.
DrMundo.fight: Before fighting, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. If Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases is available, use tornado Q to remove it first, then look for a knock-up with Yone R Fate Sealed. While staying close, use Yone W Spirit Cleave to gain both a shield and damage based on maximum health.
DrMundo.laning: Avoid pushing the wave with repeated Q casts, and save Yone E Soul Unbound if you don’t know where the enemy jungler is. Dodge Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw with minions between you, and after trading, retreat along a path that lets you step on a canister Dr. Mundo dropped.
DrMundo.phase: Take the initiative in fights as soon as you complete your first core item with attack speed and critical strike. Even later, while Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is available, look for gains in other lanes or at objectives instead of spending time trying to kill him.
DrMundo.teamfight: Use Yone E Soul Unbound to pressure the backline and return safely. Hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, and use Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team. Hold R if the angle would send you deep into the enemy team after passing through multiple enemies.
DrMundo.watch: Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw hits only the first target and deals damage based on current health, so when your health is high, stand behind minions to dodge it. When the basic attack empowered by Dr. Mundo E Blunt Force Trauma is about to hit, time Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield to meet it. When Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is active, his healing and movement speed increase, so don’t commit to a kill.

Ekko.build: Prioritize attack speed and critical strike toward completing your first core item. Build magic resistance rather than armor against Ekko’s damage. If the healing from Ekko R Chronobreak can turn the duel, buy Executioner's Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Ekko.combo: Before fighting, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. When Ekko W Parallel Convergence is down and he can’t use Ekko R Chronobreak, deal damage in this order: Yone E Soul Unbound → tornado Q Mortal Steel → basic attack → W Spirit Cleave → R Fate Sealed → basic attack. Afterward, recast Yone E Soul Unbound to return to your starting position.
Ekko.escape: If only Ekko E Phase Dive is down, he can still escape with Ekko R Chronobreak, so don’t keep chasing. Close the gap with Yone Q Mortal Steel and E Soul Unbound during the window when both Ekko W Parallel Convergence and R Chronobreak are down.
Ekko.fight: Avoid the area when you see the tell for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, and look for a chance to knock Ekko up with prepared Yone Q Mortal Steel tornado right after he closes in with Ekko E Phase Dive. The opportunity to commit is after Ekko R Chronobreak is down. Don’t use Yone E Soul Unbound to dive deep into an area where Ekko W Parallel Convergence is available.
Ekko.laning: When Ekko Q Timewinder flies toward you, avoid its return path. When you see the tell for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, move outside its area. If you don’t know where the jungler is, avoid pushing the lane too far by farming with Q and save Yone E Soul Unbound.
Ekko.phase: Take the initiative in fights as soon as you complete your first core item with attack speed and critical strike. The available information isn’t enough to determine which champion has the advantage in the late game; look for opportunities when Ekko R Chronobreak is down.
Ekko.teamfight: Engage with Yone E Soul Unbound to pressure the backline, then return. Hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, and use R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team. Right after Ekko closes in with E Phase Dive, look for a chance to knock him up with Yone Q Mortal Steel or R Fate Sealed and force out Ekko R Chronobreak.
Ekko.watch: When you see the tell for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, stay out of its area to avoid the stun and shield. Ekko Q Timewinder deals more damage on its return, so move away from its return path. If you see Ekko’s afterimage, Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, so don’t chase recklessly even when health is low.

Fiora.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Fiora Q Lunge and Fiora E Bladework. If the healing from Fiora P Duelist's Dance and Fiora R Grand Challenge can turn the duel, buy Executioner's Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Fiora.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. Once Fiora W Riposte is down, trade briefly in this order: tornado Q → two basic attacks → Yone W Spirit Cleave → basic attack. For an all-in, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, then deal damage in this order: tornado Q → basic attack → W → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack. Recast E to return.
Fiora.escape: Right after making Fiora use Q Lunge is your chance to close the gap. If Fiora W Riposte is also down, engage with the tornado from Yone Q Mortal Steel or with Yone E Soul Unbound. If Riposte is available, don’t open with a knock-up.
Fiora.fight: After Fiora W Riposte is down, trade briefly with a prepared tornado Q after hitting a minion with Yone Q Mortal Steel. Right after making Fiora use Q Lunge, close the gap with Yone E Soul Unbound, avoid giving her a vital, hit only as much as needed, then retreat.
Fiora.laning: Stand opposite the side where a vital appears and use the moment Fiora moves in that direction as a chance to counterattack. If you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, avoid pushing the lane too far by farming with Q and save Yone E Soul Unbound.
Fiora.phase: Once your first core item is complete and you have attack speed and critical strike, Yone can take the initiative in fights.
Fiora.teamfight: Use Yone E Soul Unbound to pressure the backline and return safely. Hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, and use Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team. If Fiora R Grand Challenge hits you, stay near a wall so you don’t expose all four vitals.
Fiora.watch: Fiora W Riposte blocks attacks and immobilizing effects. If it blocks the knock-up from Yone Q Mortal Steel or Yone R Fate Sealed, it also stuns you. While Riposte is available, don’t engage first with tornado Q or R; watch for Fiora to move toward a vital or use Fiora Q Lunge, then look for an opening in her movement.

Fizz.build: Magic resistance is the resistance to build against the magic damage from Fizz W Seastone Trident, Fizz E Playful / Trickster, and Fizz R Chum the Waters. The specific first item isn’t provided.
Fizz.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. Once Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first and engage with tornado Q. Deal damage in this order: basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack. Then recast E to return. For a short trade, knock him up with tornado Q, then land two basic attacks, W, and a basic attack before retreating.
Fizz.escape: Your window to engage is after Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down and before it comes back. Fizz Q Urchin Strike is also a mobility ability, so don’t chase deep just because he used E. Don’t dive deep with Yone E Soul Unbound where Fizz R Chum the Waters can threaten you with crowd control.
Fizz.fight: Trade right after Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down by hitting him with the tornado from Yone Q Mortal Steel. There’s also an opening when Fizz W Seastone Trident’s empowered basic attack fails to secure a last hit and goes on its full cooldown. Time Yone W Spirit Cleave to shield yourself when Fizz’s main damage comes in.
Fizz.laning: If you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, don’t keep pushing the wave with Q; save Yone E Soul Unbound. If Fizz has pushed the wave, look for an angle to close in with tornado Q, but trade only after Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down.
Fizz.phase: In the mid game, Yone can take the initiative in fights once he has attack speed and critical strike and completes his first core item. The available information isn’t enough to determine who has the advantage in the late game; in teamfights, focus on drawing out Fizz E Playful / Trickster and returning safely.
Fizz.teamfight: Stand close to your team and make Fizz use E Playful / Trickster first, then focus him down. Engage with Yone E Soul Unbound active, and hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Choose an angle for Yone R Fate Sealed that pulls enemies toward your team, and hold it if the angle would send you deep into the enemy team after passing through them.
Fizz.watch: Fizz E Playful / Trickster can be used both to engage and disengage, so don’t engage first with the tornado from Yone Q Mortal Steel or Yone R Fate Sealed while it’s available. If Fizz R Chum the Waters attaches to you, move away from your teammates before the shark erupts. Watch Fizz’s engage path, since he can use Q Urchin Strike to engage as the shark knocks you up.

Galio.build: Galio’s main damage is magic damage, so build magic resistance rather than armor. Galio Q Winds of War deals damage based on maximum health, so be careful about choosing to stack health alone.
Galio.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. During the window after Galio’s taunt and knock-up are down, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first. Engage with tornado Q and deal damage in this order: basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack. Recast E to return. For a short trade, knock him up with tornado Q, then land two basic attacks, W, and a basic attack before retreating.
Galio.escape: Don’t dive deep just because Galio E Justice Punch is down. Your window to engage is after Galio W Shield of Durand’s taunt and E’s knock-up are down, and before Galio R Hero's Entrance comes back. Yone E Soul Unbound won’t return you if you’re hit by crowd control, so confirm that window before activating it.
Galio.fight: Early on, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado, but don’t engage first while Galio W Shield of Durand and E Justice Punch are available. Once Galio W Shield of Durand is down and you’ve dodged Galio E Justice Punch, use your prepared tornado to knock him up and trade briefly. Time Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield to block Galio’s key ability as it hits.
Galio.laning: After Galio spends mana clearing the wave with his abilities, push the lane to limit his opportunity to affect other lanes with Galio R Hero's Entrance. If you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, avoid pushing the lane too far by farming with Q and save Yone E Soul Unbound.
Galio.phase: Yone can fight more proactively once he completes his first core item and has attack speed and critical strike. The available information isn’t enough to determine who has the advantage in the late game, so base your fights on whether Galio has used his crowd control and mobility abilities.
Galio.teamfight: While Galio R Hero's Entrance is ready, don’t initiate skirmishes with Galio’s team, even in other lanes. Move outside the area when the landing marker appears. Use Yone E Soul Unbound to pressure the backline, and hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Use Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team, and hold it if the angle would send you deep into the enemy team after passing through them.
Galio.watch: When Galio charges W Shield of Durand, he takes reduced damage and prepares a taunt, so don’t pour in your damage; move out of range. Dodge Galio E Justice Punch when you see its wind-up as he steps back, and move out of the point where both gusts from Galio Q Winds of War overlap. If you see the landing marker for Galio R Hero's Entrance, immediately move outside its area.

Gangplank.build: Build armor first, starting in the laning phase, since Gangplank Q Parrrley and E Powder Keg deal his main physical damage. Also consider your total health, since resistance can’t block the true damage from Gangplank P Trial by Fire and R Cannon Barrage. If the healing from Gangplank W Remove Scurvy can turn the duel, buy Executioner's Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Gangplank.combo: Before fighting, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. If Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down and E Powder Keg has just been placed, deal damage in this order: Yone E Soul Unbound → tornado Q → basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack. Recast E to return. For a short trade, knock him up with tornado Q, land two basic attacks and W, then retreat.
Gangplank.escape: Gangplank has no ability to create distance on his own, so engage when there are no primed Gangplank E Powder Kegs nearby and Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down. If W Remove Scurvy is available, delay any engage intended to secure a guaranteed kill with the knock-ups from Yone Q Mortal Steel and R Fate Sealed.
Gangplank.fight: Trade right after Gangplank E Powder Keg is placed, before the barrel is primed. If there’s a primed barrel nearby, back off first.
Gangplank.laning: Q can push the wave, so if you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, use it less to farm, pull the lane toward you, and save Yone E Soul Unbound. If Gangplank has pushed the lane and there are no primed barrels nearby, look for an angle to trade with tornado Q.
Gangplank.phase: Once your first core item is complete and you have attack speed and critical strike, Yone can take the initiative in fights. The available information isn’t enough to determine the relative advantage in the late game.
Gangplank.teamfight: Go deep into the backline only with Yone E Soul Unbound active, and hit multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield. Use Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team, and hold it if the angle would send you deep into the enemy team after passing through multiple enemies. Time objective fights based on whether Gangplank R Cannon Barrage has been used.
Gangplank.watch: Back off if Gangplank E Powder Keg is primed, and don’t enter an area where two barrels overlap. Destroy barrels from outside their blast radius. In situations where Gangplank Q Parrrley is chipping away at health, time Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield to block key poke. Gangplank P Trial by Fire and R Cannon Barrage deal true damage, so be especially careful when health is low.

Garen.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Garen Q Decisive Strike and Garen E Judgment. Also consider your total health, since resistance can’t reduce the true damage from Garen R Demacian Justice. If the healing from Garen P Perseverance can turn the duel, buy Executioner's Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder.
Garen.combo: After Garen Q Decisive Strike has been fully spent and Garen W Courage’s brief defensive window has passed, engage with the tornado you’ve built on minions using Yone Q Mortal Steel. Trade in this order: two basic attacks → Yone W Spirit Cleave → basic attack. For an all-in, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first, engage with tornado Q, then land a basic attack, W, Yone R Fate Sealed, and a basic attack. Recast E to return.
Garen.escape: Garen has no ability to create distance on his own, so close the gap with Yone Q Mortal Steel and Yone E Soul Unbound when Garen Q Decisive Strike’s empowered basic attack is consumed. If Garen has just activated W Courage, don’t immediately use the knock-up from Yone Q Mortal Steel or Yone R Fate Sealed; wait for its brief defensive window to pass.
Garen.fight: Trade briefly right after Garen Q Decisive Strike is used on a minion or its empowered basic attack is consumed. Don’t stay in range of Garen E Judgment’s spin for long; hit for as long as you planned, then retreat.
Garen.laning: Afterward, pressure Garen to limit the time he has to build permanent stacks for W Courage. If you don’t know where the enemy jungler is, farm less with Q to pull the lane toward you and save Yone E Soul Unbound. After pushing the lane out, create a numbers advantage elsewhere.
Garen.phase: Once you have attack speed and your first core item, Yone W Spirit Cleave gives you better defense and damage, so take the initiative in fights. You become more disadvantaged over time because of Garen W Courage’s permanent stacks, so pressure him early to limit his opportunities to build them.
Garen.teamfight: Use Yone E Soul Unbound to pressure the enemy backline and return safely. Clip multiple enemies with Yone W Spirit Cleave to build a larger shield, and use Yone R Fate Sealed to pull enemies toward your team. Hold R if the angle would send you deep into the enemy team after passing through multiple enemies.
Garen.watch: Garen Q Decisive Strike’s empowered basic attack silences you and prevents you from counterattacking, so don’t engage first while it’s active. When Garen E Judgment starts, move out of its spin range. Right after Garen W Courage, delay the knock-ups from Yone Q Mortal Steel and Yone R Fate Sealed by half a beat. If your health is below half, don’t stay within range of Garen R Demacian Justice, which deals true damage based on your missing health.

Gnar.build: Build armor first against Gnar’s main physical damage. Armor won’t block the magic damage from Gnar W Hyper / Wallop, so consider magic resistance if needed. Be wary of stacking health alone because of his damage based on maximum health.
Gnar.combo: Hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. Once Gnar E Hop / Crunch is down, activate Yone E Soul Unbound first. Knock him up with tornado Q and deal damage in this order: basic attack → Yone W Spirit Cleave → Yone R Fate Sealed → basic attack. Then recast E to return. If Gnar still has a way to immobilize you, don’t rush the tornado Q and E engage.
Gnar.escape: Right after making Gnar use E Hop / Crunch is your window to close the gap with Yone Q Mortal Steel and Yone E Soul Unbound. Don’t dive deep with E near a wall where Mega Gnar R GNAR! could stun you. Look for an all-in right after Mega Gnar returns to Mini Gnar, while he can’t transform again.
Gnar.fight: Fight when you can get on Mini Gnar, and use the moment right after Gnar uses E Hop / Crunch as your chance to engage. Before fighting, hit minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare a tornado. Once you’re close, use Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield to absorb Gnar’s key damage. Immediately after he transforms into Mega Gnar, create distance and let time pass.
